Thanksgiving Hymn of the Restored and Converted Jews.</title> <div sID="gen13942" type="x-p"/> Just as Miriam, after the deliverance of the Red Sea (<reference osisRef="Isa.11.16">Is 11:16</reference>), celebrated it with an ode of praise (<reference osisRef="Exod.15.1-Exod.15.19">Ex 15:1-19</reference>).<div eID="gen13942" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13943" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8543"/><hi type="bold">2. Lord Jehovah--</hi>Jah, Jehovah. The repetition of the name denotes emphasis, and the unchangeableness of God's character.<div eID="gen13943" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13944" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">strength ... song ... salvation--</hi>derived from <reference osisRef="Exod.15.2">Ex 15:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.118.14">Psa 118:14</reference>. The idea of salvation was peculiarly associated with the feast of tabernacles (see <reference osisRef="Isa.12.3">Is 12:3</reference>). Hence the cry "Hosanna," "Save, we beseech thee," that accompanied Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem on that day (the fifteenth of the seventh month) (<reference osisRef="Matt.21.9">Mt 21:9</reference>; compare with <reference osisRef="Ps.118.25">Psa 118:25</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.118.26">26</reference>); the earnest of the perfected "salvation" which He shall bring to His people at His glorious second appearance at Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Heb.9.28">He 9:28</reference>). "He shall appear the second time without sin unto salvation." Compare <reference osisRef="Rev.21.3">Re 21:3</reference>, "The tabernacle of God is with men." Compare <reference osisRef="Luke.9.33">Lu 9:33</reference>, "three tabernacles: one for thee," &c. (the transfiguration being a pledge of the future kingdom), (<reference osisRef="Ps.118.15">Psa 118:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.16">Zec 14:16</reference>). As the Jew was reminded by the feast of tabernacles of his wanderings in tents in the wilderness, so the Jew-Gentile Church to come shall call to mind, with thanksgiving, the various past ways whereby God has at last brought them to the heavenly "city of habitation" (<reference osisRef="Ps.107.7">Psa 107:7</reference>). <div eID="gen13944" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8544"/><div sID="gen13945" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8544"/><hi type="bold">3. draw water ... salvation--</hi>an expressive image in a hot country. On the last day of the feast of tabernacles the Jews used to bring water in a golden pitcher from the fountain of Siloam, and pour it, mingled with wine, on the sacrifice on the altar, with great rejoicing. This is the allusion in Jesus' words on "the last day of the feast" (<reference osisRef="John.7.2">Joh 7:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="John.7.37-John.7.39">37-39</reference>). The pouring out of water indicated repentance (<reference osisRef="1Sam.7.6">1Sa 7:6</reference>; compare, as to the Jews' repentance hereafter, <reference osisRef="Zech.12.10">Zec 12:10</reference>). There shall be a latter outpouring of the Spirit like the former one on pentecost (<reference osisRef="Joel.2.23">Joe 2:23</reference>).<div eID="gen13945" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13946" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">wells--</hi>not mere streams, which may run dry, but ever-flowing fountains (<reference osisRef="John.4.14">Joh 4:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.7.38">7:38</reference>), "Out of his belly (that is, in and from himself)--living water" (<reference osisRef="Isa.42.18">Is 42:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.84.6">Psa 84:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.13.1">Zec 13:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.7.17">Re 7:17</reference>). <div eID="gen13946" type="x-p"/>
